comment: Findings against crates that the Wasmtime C API library links, and that
pkg/contrib cannot resolve by bumping the pin.  check-lock-audit.py fails
the audit on any other linked finding.  A finding outside the linked graph
needs no entry here; it is reported and ignored.
The version is part of the key, so a pin bump forces this file to be
reviewed again rather than carrying an acceptance forward silently.

allow.reason: Linked through rand 0.10.1, which wasmtime-wasi uses to seed guest randomness. A yank is not an advisory: no RustSec record applies to this version in the audited database. The Wasmtime 48.0.7 archive is vendored and its lock still names chacha20 0.10.0, so it cannot be updated independently of the source pin.

Linked by the Wasmtime 48.0.7 C API even with component-model, component-model-async and wasi-http disabled. RUSTSEC-2026-0386 concerns safe AsyncFd constructors accepting AsRawFd without guaranteeing a valid, owned and unchanged descriptor. All 245 linked package source trees other than Tokio, including Wasmtime, contain no AsyncFd callers; Tokio's own AsyncFd implementation is not used by this build. The source archive is vendored, so this exact version cannot be updated independently of the source pin. Recheck reachability and remove this exception at the next pin bump.

Linked by the Wasmtime 48.0.7 C API through wasmtime_byteorder. RUSTSEC-2026-0403 (also listed as an unsound warning) concerns uninitialized memory exposure during streaming decompression of a legacy frame. The Wasmtime 48.0.7 source archive is vendored and its Cargo.lock cannot be repaired in-tree, so this exact version cannot be updated independently of the source pin. Recheck reachability and remove this exception at the next pin bump.
